subdomain.description: The workspace part of your NeetoCal address, for example spinkart.
subdomain.title: Workspace Subdomain

NeetoCalAPIKeyCredential.title: NeetoCal API Key
NeetoCalAPIKeyCredential.x-credential-instructions: Create a workspace API key in NeetoCal's Admin Panel → API keys. Paste the key and your workspace subdomain, for example spinkart for spinkart.neetocal.com. NoClick sends X-Api-Key only to this workspace's NeetoCal API.

meeting_slug.description: Slug of scheduling link you want to book.
meeting_slug.title: Meeting Slug

name.description: Name of person making the booking.
name.title: Name

email.description: Email of person making the booking.
email.title: Email

slot_date.description: Date on which you want to book. This should be in "YYYY-MM-DD" format. If `slot_date` and `slot_start_time` are not provided then the first available slot will be booked. Both are required when `override_availability` is `true`.
slot_date.title: Slot Date

slot_start_time.description: Start time for the booking. This should be in "HH:MM AM/PM" format.
slot_start_time.title: Slot Start Time

time_zone.description: Time zone of person making the booking.
time_zone.title: Time Zone

preferred_meeting_spot.description: Your preferred meeting place. This field is optional. Before passing this value, ensure that the corresponding meeting place is configured in the "Where" section of the scheduling link.
preferred_meeting_spot.title: Preferred Meeting Spot

form_responses.description: Responses for the questions of booking form (optional). The key of the field should be the field code of the question. The field code can be found in scheduling link's Settings -> Questions -> 3 dot menu of the question -> Edit -> Advanced properties. You can specify guest emails using the `guest_email_s` field code.
form_responses.title: Form Responses

add_on_service_ids.description: IDs of the [add-on services](/api/add-on-services/list) to include in the booking. The booking's duration and the amount charged include the chosen add-on services. When `slot_date` and `slot_start_time` are omitted, the first slot long enough for the add-on services is booked. Returns a 422 error if an ID does not belong to the scheduling link, or if more than one is passed while the scheduling link's `allow_multiple_add_on_services` is `false`.
add_on_service_ids.title: Add On Service Ids

host_email.description: Email of the host to assign the booking to, for scheduling links with more than one host. Allowed only when `override_availability` is `true` or the scheduling link lets clients choose the host. When omitted, the host is assigned automatically. You can get the host emails from the `hosts` array in the [Get scheduling link](/api/scheduling-links/get) response.
host_email.title: Host Email

slug.description: Slug of the scheduling link. This value should be unique.
slug.title: Slug

hosts.description: Emails of the hosts of scheduling link in array format.
hosts.title: Hosts

duration.description: Duration of the scheduling link in minutes.
duration.title: Duration

start_time_increment.description: Start time increment for the scheduling link in minutes. Defaults to 30.
start_time_increment.title: Start Time Increment

before_buffer_time.description: Buffer time in minutes before each meeting to allow for setup, preparation, or travel time. Must be between 0 and 1440 (24 hours).
before_buffer_time.title: Before Buffer Time

after_buffer_time.description: Buffer time in minutes after each meeting to allow for wrap-up, notes, or preparation for the next meeting. Must be between 0 and 1440 (24 hours).
after_buffer_time.title: After Buffer Time

locked_time_zone.description: Time zone to lock the scheduling link to. When set, all available times are displayed in this time zone regardless of the booker's location. Must be a valid IANA time zone identifier (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London').
locked_time_zone.title: Locked Time Zone

name.description: Name of person making the booking. This is applied only as part of a reschedule, so send it alongside `slot_date` and `slot_start_time`. A request carrying it without them is rejected with a 422 error.
name.title: Name

email.description: Email of person making the booking. This is applied only as part of a reschedule, so send it alongside `slot_date` and `slot_start_time`. A request carrying it without them is rejected with a 422 error.
email.title: Email

slot_date.description: Date on which the booking is to be rescheduled. This should be in "YYYY-MM-DD" format.
slot_date.title: Slot Date

slot_start_time.description: Start time for the booking. This should be in "HH:MM AM/PM" format.
slot_start_time.title: Slot Start Time

time_zone.description: Time zone of person rescheduling the booking.
time_zone.title: Time Zone

status.description: Sets booking lifecycle status in one call (replaces v1 approve / reject / cancel endpoints). Use `approved` to approve, `rejected` to reject (optional `rejection_reason`), or `cancelled` to cancel (optional `cancel_reason`). Do not send this field when you are only rescheduling or updating other attributes.
status.title: Status

cancel_reason.description: Reason for cancelling the booking. Used when status is `cancelled`.
cancel_reason.title: Cancel Reason

rejection_reason.description: Reason for rejecting the booking. Used when status is `rejected`.
rejection_reason.title: Rejection Reason

meeting_outcome_id.description: Assign a meeting outcome to the booking by providing the outcome's ID. Pass `null` to remove the currently assigned outcome. This parameter cannot be combined with `status` or reschedule parameters (`slot_date`, `slot_start_time`) in the same request. Meeting outcomes can only be set on confirmed or parallel-error bookings. You can get the outcome ID from the [List meeting outcomes](/api/meeting-outcomes/list) endpoint.
meeting_outcome_id.title: Meeting Outcome Id

ScheduleConfig.description:
Schedule configuration from the frontend widget.
Fields accept Union[int, str] to support drag-and-drop references like
{{nodeId.values.field}} which get resolved at configuration time.

daysOfWeek.description: Days of week to run on (0=Sunday … 6=Saturday); empty = every day. Supported for seconds/minutes/hours intervals and daily schedules.
daysOfWeek.title: Daysofweek

windowStart.description: Part-of-day start as 24-hour "HH:MM" in the schedule timezone (e.g. "09:00"). Set together with windowEnd; interval frequencies only.
windowStart.title: Windowstart

windowEnd.description: Part-of-day end as 24-hour "HH:MM", inclusive — a run landing exactly on it fires (e.g. "18:00" runs the 6:00 PM tick).
windowEnd.title: Windowend

monthDayStart.description: Part-of-month start day (1-31), inclusive. Set together with monthDayEnd; a start after the end wraps around month end (25→5 = the 25th through the 5th).
monthDayStart.title: Monthdaystart

monthStart.description: Part-of-year start month (1=January … 12=December), inclusive. Set together with monthEnd; a start after the end wraps around the new year (11→2 = November through February).
monthStart.title: Monthstart

ScheduleConfig.title: ScheduleConfig

credentials.description: Credentials for this node (optional if using environment variables)
